title: Rust and Python routers deliver in-transit RH3 packets locally on outer-dst match; C router forwards per RFC 6554
description: Confirmed empirically by the security codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-njdx (live Router.route probe). In-transit source-routed packets (Routing header with segments_left != 0, outer dst = this node, UDP checksum validly over the RFC 2460 s8.1 final destination) are LOCALLY DELIVERED by Rust (lichen-node/src/stack.rs:562-566 delivers when ipv6_destination_is_local_or_multicast, which reads only bytes 24..40 with no segments-left check; lichen-schc/src/link.rs:184-193 admits on L2 destination alone) and Python (lichen/routing/router.py:474-476 returns DELIVER_LOCAL on outer-dst match; node.py:978-982 hands it to the app). C honors forwarding precedence: lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/router.c:504-522 forwards and never delivers while segments_left != 0, and additionally rejects at router level what the P/R gates admit: RH3 final address equal to outer dst (router.c:400-402), misaligned address grids, and multiple Routing headers (saw_routing) — Rust/Python have no router-level SRH validation at all (RFC 8200 s4.4 processes only the first Routing header; P/R gates accept a second one and derive checksum scope last-wins). Attack: an authenticated neighbor unicasts outer-dst=victim + RH3 SL=1 to any final -> the victim Rust/Python node consumes the datagram C would only relay; same wire bytes, opposite fate; downward RPL source-routed traffic silently terminates at the first Rust/Python relay. Fix direction: before local delivery, reject/deliver-local only when no Routing header has segments_left != 0 (mirror router.c), add router-level SRH validation (final != outer dst when SL!=0, single RH3, aligned address grid) to Rust and Python, and pin with cross-impl admission vectors. Related gate-level context: the SCHC-gate last-wins multi-RH acceptance is consistent P<->R (no gate-level bypass), recorded here for the router fix.
